name: René Pijnen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 100km team time trial at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics at age 22, having also won bronze in the amateur road race at the 1967 UCI Road World Championships at age 21.
early_history_summary: Pijnen debuted as a novice cyclist in 1963 at age 17, winning 40 of 98 road races in that category. As an amateur he accumulated 49 road victories, including the overall classification at the Scottish Milk Race and stages in Belgium and Luxembourg, before winning Olympic gold in 1968 and turning professional in 1969.
secondary_engine: Early specialization in Dutch cycling culture
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Woensdrecht, Netherlands.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early competitive reps, Dutch cycling ecosystem, time-trial talent, team time trial partnership
evidence_summary: Pijnen began racing at 17 and rapidly dominated the novice category, winning 40 of 98 races. By 21 he had bronze at the World Amateur Road Championships and by 22 he was an Olympic gold medalist in the team time trial. No family background or coaching relationships are documented in reviewed sources. His advantage appears to be self-created domain repetition within the strong Dutch cycling culture, combined with natural time-trial ability.
starting_point: Born in Woensdrecht, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired former professional cyclist; ran a hotel near his birthplace after retirement. Born 1946 and believed living.

trajectory.event: Debuted as a novice cyclist, winning 40 of 98 road races in the beginner category.
Won bronze in the amateur road race at the UCI Road World Championships and overall classification at the Scottish Milk Race.
Won Olympic gold in the 100km team time trial at the Mexico City Olympics and finished fifth in the individual road race.
Won three stages of the Vuelta a España and held the race leader's jersey for multiple days.
Won silver in the individual pursuit at the UCI Track World Championships.
Retired from professional cycling after a career spanning 72 six-day race victories and six European madison championships.

name: Kong Linghui
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold in men's singles and team at the 1995 World Table Tennis Championships at age 20, and also won the 1995 World Cup singles title the same year.
early_history_summary: Kong learned table tennis at age 6, influenced by his father Kong Xiangzhi, a table tennis coach in Harbin. He joined the Heilongjiang provincial youth team at 10, the provincial team at 11, the national youth team at 13, and the full national team at 16. He won the National Junior Tournament singles title at 14 and the World Youth Championships singles at 19.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization in Chinese national table tennis pipeline
family_context_summary: Born in Harbin, Heilongjiang, China; father Kong Xiangzhi was a table tennis coach in Harbin. Kong grew up around the provincial sports team compound from age 3, immersed in table tennis environments.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a table tennis coach who provided early immersion in the sport, though Kong himself initiated training at age 6 by his own decision. Father deliberately ensured no special treatment in training environments.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father table tennis coach, Chinese national team pipeline, early immersion from age 3, provincial to national team progression, dedicated coaching
evidence_summary: Kong Linghui was immersed in table tennis from age 3 through his father's coaching role, began formal training at 6, and progressed through the Chinese national team pipeline to reach the full national team at 16. His father was a table tennis coach who provided domain knowledge and early access to provincial sports facilities. By 20 he was world champion in singles and team, and by 21 he was Olympic champion in doubles. The Chinese national team system provided elite coaching, peer competition, and structural support.
starting_point: Born in Harbin, Heilongjiang, China; father Kong Xiangzhi was a table tennis coach, providing early immersion in the sport from age 3.
current_position: Former head coach of China's national women's table tennis team; retired from active coaching role. Believed living as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won the National Junior Tournament singles title, marking his emergence as a top junior player.
Promoted to the Chinese national table tennis team.
Won World Championship gold in men's singles and team, plus the World Cup singles title.
Won Olympic gold in men's doubles with Liu Guoliang at the Atlanta Olympics.
Won Olympic gold in men's singles at the Sydney Olympics, defeating Jan-Ove Waldner in the final.
Became coach of China's national women's table tennis team.

name: Martin Hansson
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hansson started refereeing at 15 but only reached the Swedish Superettan in 1996 (age 25) and the Allsvenskan in 1999 (age 28). His FIFA listing came in 2001 at age 30, with major assignments (Confederations Cup final 2009, World Cup 2010) arriving much later.
early_history_summary: Hansson began refereeing at age 15 at his local club in Holmsjö, Sweden. He gradually progressed through Swedish football's refereeing tiers, reaching the second-tier Superettan by 1996 and the top-flight Allsvenskan by 1999.
evidence_summary: Hansson started refereeing at 15 and progressed gradually through Swedish football leagues. His FIFA badge came at 30 and his major assignments (Confederations Cup final, World Cup) came in his late 30s. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Bertrand Blier
milestone_by_age_26: Directed his first feature documentary film 'Hitler? Connais pas!' in 1963 at age 24, which was banned for under-18s and withdrawn from the Cannes Film Festival, giving him his first public notoriety.
early_history_summary: Blier was the son of actor Bernard Blier and pianist Gisèle Brunet. He decided to become a filmmaker at 16 after meeting his father's friend, director Henri-Georges Clouzot. He worked as an assistant director on films by Lautner, Christian-Jaque, and Delannoy from 1960 to 1963 before making his directorial debut.
family_context_summary: Born in Boulogne-Billancourt, France, to actor Bernard Blier and pianist Gisèle Brunet. His father was a well-known French actor who was shooting Marcel Carné's 'Le Jour se Lève' when Bertrand was born.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Bernard Blier was a prominent French film actor, providing direct access to the French film industry. Blier met director Henri-Georges Clouzot through his father at age 16, which inspired his career direction.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father was famous actor, French cinema network, met Clouzot at 16, assistant director reps, Paris film ecosystem
evidence_summary: Blier grew up in a French cinema family: his father Bernard Blier was a prominent actor, and his mother was a pianist. He met director Henri-Georges Clouzot through his father at 16, which set him on the path to filmmaking. He worked as an assistant director from 1960-63 before directing his first feature at 24. The film was banned for under-18s and withdrawn from Cannes, giving him early notoriety. His access to the French film industry through his father was a direct and catalytic advantage.
starting_point: Born in Boulogne-Billancourt, France; son of actor Bernard Blier and pianist Gisèle Brunet, growing up immersed in the French film industry.
current_position: Died on January 20, 2025 at age 85 in Paris; final film was made in 2019. Career spanned Oscar-winning films including 'Get Out Your Handkerchiefs' (1978) and Cannes Grand Prize winner 'Too Beautiful for You' (1989).

trajectory.event: Directed first feature documentary 'Hitler? Connais pas!' which was banned for under-18s and withdrawn from Cannes, earning him early notoriety.
Directed 'Going Places' (Les Valseuses), his breakthrough feature film starring Gérard Depardieu.
'Get Out Your Handkerchiefs' won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
Won the Grand Prize at the Cannes Film Festival for 'Too Beautiful for You' (Trop belle pour toi).
Died on January 20, 2025 at his home in Paris.

name: William Anders
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Anders graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1955 (age 22) and earned his pilot's wings in 1956. At 26 he was a graduate student at the Air Force Institute of Technology studying nuclear engineering. He was selected by NASA in 1963 at age 30 and flew on Apollo 8 in 1968 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Anders graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1955 and was commissioned into the U.S. Air Force, earning his pilot's wings in 1956. He served as an all-weather fighter interceptor pilot before entering the AFIT graduate program in 1958 to study nuclear engineering.
family_context_summary: Born in Hong Kong to U.S. Navy lieutenant Arthur Ferdinand Anders and Muriel Adams Anders. The family moved frequently due to his father's naval postings, including to Nanjing, China, before returning to the United States.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a U.S. Navy officer serving on the Yangtze River Patrol, providing a military family background but not directly in aerospace.
evidence_summary: Anders had a military family background and attended the U.S. Naval Academy, graduating at 22. By 26 he was a graduate student in nuclear engineering. His NASA selection came at 30 and his Apollo 8 mission at 35. No material public milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Dieter Schwarz
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Schwarz joined his father Josef's fruit wholesale business after marrying in 1963. He and his father opened their first supermarket (Handelshof) in 1968 when Schwarz was 29, and the first Lidl discount store opened in 1973 when he was 34.
early_history_summary: Schwarz was born in Heilbronn, Germany, to Josef Schwarz, who had been a partner in the fruit wholesaler Suedfruechte Grosshandel Lidl & Co. since 1930. Dieter married in 1963 and joined the family business, but did not open his own retail store until 1968 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Born in Heilbronn, Germany; father Josef Schwarz was a partner in the Suedfruechte Grosshandel Lidl & Co. fruit wholesale business since 1930. The family had a wholesale/retail business background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Josef Schwarz was in the fruit wholesale and retail business, providing Dieter with a family business platform in the grocery trade.
evidence_summary: Schwarz inherited a family fruit wholesale business from his father Josef, but did not open his own retail store until age 29 (1968) and the first Lidl store until age 34 (1973). While he had a family business platform, no material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was identified. He became CEO only after his father's death in 1977.

name: Agnes Simon
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold in women's doubles at the 1957 World Table Tennis Championships in Stockholm at age 22, having previously won team bronze (1953, age 18) and team silver (1954, age 19) at the World Championships.
early_history_summary: Simon (née Almási) was born in Budapest and began playing table tennis at Budapesti Vasas club from 1950 at age 15. She was a member of the Hungarian champion team from 1952 to 1955 and won the Hungarian doubles championship in 1953, earning a spot on the national team. She competed at the World Championships from 1953 onward, winning team bronze at 18 and team silver at 19 before her doubles gold at 22.
primary_leverage_engine: Early specialization in Hungarian table tennis system
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Budapest, Hungary. Her husband Béla Simon was also her coach and they fled Hungary together after the 1956 revolution.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Husband Béla Simon served as her coach but this relationship began before the 1956 defection.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian table tennis system, Budapesti Vasas club, early international competition from age 15, doubles partnership, defection and rebuilding
evidence_summary: Simon began playing table tennis at 15 at Budapesti Vasas club in Budapest and quickly rose through the Hungarian system, winning national team championships from 1952-1955. She competed at the World Championships starting at age 15, winning team bronze at 18, team silver at 19, and doubles gold at 22. After the 1956 Hungarian Revolution she fled with her husband/coach Béla Simon, eventually settling in the Netherlands and then West Germany, where she continued her career and won multiple European titles. No family background is documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Budapest, Hungary; family background not documented in reviewed sources. Began playing at Budapesti Vasas club at age 15.
current_position: Died on August 19, 2020 at age 85 after a short illness. Was active in Bundesliga table tennis until age 60 and led her Duisburg club to 18 German team championships.

trajectory.event: Won World Championship team bronze for Hungary at Bucharest and Hungarian national doubles championship.
Won World Championship team silver for Hungary at London.
Won World Championship gold in women's doubles with Livia Mossóczy at Stockholm.
Won European Championship gold in singles and team for West Germany, plus silver in doubles and mixed doubles.
Won European Championship team gold for West Germany at Lyon.
Died on August 19, 2020 after a short illness.

name: Peter Chen
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Chen completed his PhD in computer science at Harvard in 1973 at age 26, but his seminal contribution — the Entity-Relationship Model — was published in 1976 at age 29. The PhD itself is an academic credential, not a material public milestone.
early_history_summary: Chen was born in Taichung, Taiwan, and graduated from National Taiwan University with a BS in electrical engineering in 1968. He pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University, earning his PhD in computer science and applied mathematics in 1973. After graduation he worked at Honeywell before joining MIT as an assistant professor in 1974.
family_context_summary: Born in Taichung, Taiwan. Inspired by An Wang to pursue doctoral studies in the United States at Harvard. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Chen earned his PhD from Harvard at 26 but his landmark ER model paper was published at 29 (1976). The PhD is an academic credential rather than a material public milestone. His influential career achievements (ER model, ACM-AAAI Allen Newell Award, IEEE Harry Goode Award) all came after age 26.

name: Eduard Artemyev
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Artemyev graduated from the Moscow Conservatory in 1960 at age 23 and began exploring electronic music. His first composition on the ANS synthesizer was written in 1967 at age 30, and his first major film score (Solaris) came in 1972 at age 35.

His career-defining collaborations with Tarkovsky and Mikhalkov came in his mid-30s onward. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

name: Viktor Belenko
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Belenko entered Soviet military service in 1967 at age 20 and qualified as a fighter pilot. His famous defection to the West with a MiG-25 aircraft occurred on September 6, 1976, when he was 29 years old.
early_history_summary: Belenko was born in Nalchik, Kabardin ASSR, Soviet Union. He entered military service in 1967 and became a fighter pilot in the Soviet Air Defence Forces. He was stationed at Chuguyevka Air Base near Vladivostok before his defection to Japan in 1976.
family_context_summary: Born in Nalchik, Russian SFSR, in a Russian family. Limited family background documented in reviewed sources. His wife Lyudmila came from a wealthy family and was seeking divorce at the time of his defection.
evidence_summary: Belenko entered Soviet military service at 20 and became a fighter pilot. His defining moment — defecting to Japan with a MiG-25 — occurred at 29 in 1976. No material milestone by age 26 was identified in reviewed sources.

name: Toshio Suzuki
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Suzuki graduated from Keio University in 1972 at age 24 and joined Tokuma Shoten as a junior editor. At 26 he was working on entertainment magazine pages. His career-defining move to Animage came in 1978 at age 30, and Studio Ghibli was co-founded in 1985 at age 37.
early_history_summary: Suzuki was born in Nagoya and studied literature at Keio University, graduating in 1972. He joined publisher Tokuma Shoten, working on the entertainment magazine Asahi Geino covering manga. In 1975 he moved to Television Land magazine, and in 1978 he became an editor at the pioneering anime magazine Animage, where he met Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata.
family_context_summary: Born in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. Family ran a small clothes-manufacturing business, where Suzuki helped as a child. His first outside job was at a rubber-making factory.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family ran a small clothes-manufacturing business, providing early exposure to manufacturing and production thinking but not directly related to film or publishing.
evidence_summary: Suzuki graduated from Keio University at 24 and joined Tokuma Shoten as a junior editor. At 26 he was editing entertainment magazine content. His pivotal career moves — joining Animage in 1978, meeting Miyazaki, and co-founding Studio Ghibli in 1985 — all came well after age 26. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.
